new_results.statement: For physical hubs H of size2 and leaves L of size3, W=A[H,L] rank2, B=A[L,L], unit nu in ker W, Gamma=det(WW^T)|nu^TBnu|>0 implies a continuous C0 density with ||p_Q||inf<16 Gamma^(-1/5), retaining arbitrary outside curvature and affine terms.

For A=D+U Lambda U^T, U^TU=I2, q_ab=det(u_a,u_b)^2, any disjoint hub pair ij and leaf triple rst with q_ij>0 and q_rs+q_rt+q_st>0 obey q_ij(det Lambda)^2|d_r q_st+d_s q_rt+d_t q_rs| < 16^5 rho^-5 for every slab ratio rho.
In the partner diffuse exact-rank2 near-null branch, ||A[k,k^c]||2 >= sqrt((1-c_k)/c_k)(|d_k|-sqrt(1536e^2)rho^-2)_+ >= sqrt2(1-sqrt(1536e^2)rho^-2)_+.

If q_ij>=eta, q_rs>=zeta and the weighted transverse diagonal sum has relative magnitude at least theta at a leaf triple containing the selected k, then min(|lambda1|,|lambda2|)<32(eta theta zeta)^(-1/4)rho^-5/4.

partner_result_actually_applied.application: Used |A_kk det Lambda|<=1536e^2 rho^-4 and its near-null/rank-one split to derive the new physical-star lower bound and combine the noncancelling chamber with the new transverse slab inequality.

unresolved_implication: Diffuse high-dimensional pair volumes may make every individual q_ij and q_rs tiny, and the signed weighted transverse currency may cancel. Need a grouped-bank aggregate version of the new five-coordinate invariant without a dimension factor.
